ELI5: Why can I sometimes feel my heartbeat in different areas of my body?

There are cells called baroreceptors that tell your brain what your blood pressure is. Your brain tracks it all the time, but through neural adaptation you do not notice it (think how you get used to a smell, same thing). A sudden change in position, clothing or whatever stimulus changes and it takes your nervous system a second to adapt. During that time you can notice it. That's the best I have without actually looking shit up.
